header:
Conformational Stability and Electronic Effects
This problem tests a systematic understanding of basic conformational analysis and the origins of molecular stability. Compare conformations accessible through bond rotation and answer in terms of steric effects, hyperconjugation, dipole-dipole interactions, electronegativity differences, and related factors.

subquestions.text_open:
For 8.1–8.3 and 8.5–8.6, describe in words the most stable conformation of each molecule shown, specifying in particular whether each substituent is equatorial or axial.
8.1
rubric: Most stable conformation: a trisubstituted nitrogen-containing six-membered ring whose skeleton lies approximately in the plane of the page. It contains three nitrogen atoms, 1 at the left, one at the upper right, and one at the lower right. Each nitrogen bears a tert-butyl (tBu) substituent, and all three tBu groups project outward from the ring. Two tBu groups are equatorial and one is axial. (2 points)

rubric: Most stable conformation: a six-membered ring containing four nitrogen atoms in an approximately chair conformation. Two adjacent N atoms lie on the left and another adjacent pair on the right; carbon atoms at the top and bottom connect the pairs. Each N bears an outward-pointing substituent. The methyl substituents on N atoms at positions 1 and 4 are equatorial, whereas those on N atoms at positions 2 and 5 are axial. (2 points)

subquestions.text_open: 8.4 Explain, in terms of steric hindrance, hyperconjugation, dipole-dipole interactions, electronegativity differences, and related effects, why the anti-staggered conformation predominates in 1,2-dihaloethanes when the halogen is Cl or Br, whereas the gauche-staggered conformation predominates when the halogen is F. (No more than 100 words.)
rubric: Cl and Br have large atomic radii. Although C-Cl and C-Br bonds are long, the atoms themselves are bulky, and bringing the two halogens close together in the gauche conformation causes strong van der Waals repulsion. (1 point)
Because F is strongly electronegative, the C-F antibonding orbital is low in energy and is a good electron acceptor. (1 point)
In the gauche conformation, a C-H bond and a C-F bond are antiperiplanar, giving effective orbital overlap that substantially lowers the system's energy. (1 point)
The two strongly polar bonds subtend an angle of 60°, producing substantial dipole-dipole repulsion. (1 point)
The stabilization from hyperconjugation exceeds the destabilization from dipole-dipole repulsion. (1 point)

Most stable conformation: an N-acyl-substituted nitrogen-containing cyclic skeleton. At the left is an acetyl fragment, $\mathrm{CH_3}$-C(=O)-N-, and to the right is a nitrogen-containing ring attached through N. The ring adopts an overall chair conformation. The acetyl group is approximately equatorial, while the methyl substituent at the $\alpha$ position to N is axial. (2 points)
